```{r readdata, echo = F, include = F}
# load data set
empro <- here::here("data", "EMPRO_data_20260506.RData")
load(empro)

#make enrollment month factor 
empro_data$enrollment_month1 = factor(empro_data$enrollment_month)

#make new variable for yes/no CRPC
empro_data$crpc_per = empro_data$cohort_empro != "mHSPC"

# add variable for not matched
empro_data$not_matched = ifelse(empro_data$subject %in% not_matched, 1, 0)

#relabel new vars
var_label(empro_data) <- list(
  enrollment_month1 = "Study visit at entry")

# read in site-level data
site_data <- read.csv("H:/GU/EMPRO/Randomization/randscheme_final.csv") %>% 
  rename(site_country = Country,
         site_timetodx = timetodx,
         site_crpc = CRPC)

# logit function for EORTC
logit_fun <- function(y, lower = 21, upper = 100, eps = 0.5) {
  # y: numeric vector, composite score in [lower, upper]
  # eps: small constant to avoid 0 and 1 on the probability scale 
  p <- (y - lower + eps) / (upper - lower + 2 * eps)
  log(p / (1 - p))
} # eps=0.5 is standard for bounded health outcomes, stabilizes values close to extremes
assign("logit_fun", logit_fun, envir = .GlobalEnv)


# back transformation if needed later
inv_logit_fun <- function(x, lower = 21, upper = 100, eps = 0.5) {
  p <- exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))
  (p * ((upper-lower) + 2 * eps) - eps + lower)
}


# analysis data set (remove exclusions)
analysis_data <- empro_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(empro_cnstdate) & enrollment_month<=45 & !is.na(cohort_empro)) %>%
  mutate(enrollment_month1 = fct_drop(enrollment_month1)) %>%
  mutate(sitenew = case_when(
    site=="Cross Cancer Institute (Alberta Health Services)" ~ "Cross Cancer Institute",
    site=="Guys St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust" ~ "Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust",
    site=="Royal Brisbane & Women’s Hospital" ~ "Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital",
    site=="St. Vincent’s Hospital Sydney" ~ "St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney",
    site=="University of Virgina (UVA)" ~ "University of Virginia", 
    site=="Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital" ~ "Queensland University of Technology",
    site=="NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital" ~ "Weill Cornell Medical Center",
    TRUE ~ site),
    ecog3 = replace_na(ecog2, "Unknown"),
    crpc_per = factor(crpc_per, levels=c("FALSE", "TRUE"), labels = c("mHSPC", "CRPC"))) %>% 
  left_join(site_data, by = c("sitenew"="sitegp")) %>% 
  mutate(# re-order - this matches the order from when they were randomized (must match constrained space file)
    sitenew = factor(sitenew,
                           levels = c("Queensland University of Technology",
                                      "Eastern Health",
                                      "St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney",
                                      "Macquarie University Hospital",
                                      "Cross Cancer Institute",
                                      "Ottawa Hospital Cancer Centre",
                                      "The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Duke Comprehensive Cancer Center",
                                      "Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center",
                                      "Weill Cornell Medical Center",
                                      "University of Virginia")),
  # transformed EORTC
    eortc_0_log = log(max(eortc_0, na.rm=TRUE) + 1 - eortc_0),
    eortc_6norm = logit_fun(eortc_6)) %>% 
  set_variable_labels(ecog3="ECOG",
                      enrollment_month1 = "Study visit at entry",

                      eortc_6norm = "EORTC at 6 mo (logit-transformed)",

# complete data at 6 mo
analysis_data2 <- analysis_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(eortc_6)) 

# patient counts
n_crpc <- analysis_data %>% filter(cohort_empro=="CRPC" & arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
n_mhspc <- analysis_data %>% filter(cohort_empro=="mHSPC" & arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
n_intervention <- analysis_data %>% filter(arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
```

## 6 Months
The composite score of EORTC QLQ-C30 at 6 months (range 21–100) was rescaled to the unit interval and logit‑transformed to account for boundedness and left‑skewness.  

The logit transformation expands values near the upper boundary of the scale. Because many patients had high scores, this leads to a visible clustering at the upper end of the transformed distribution, even though the raw scores appear smooth. This behavior is expected for bounded patient‑reported outcomes and does not indicate model misspecification.
```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}

ggplot(analysis_data, aes(x = eortc_6)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = "#a6dba0", color = "black") +
```

# Permutation test
Treatment effects were analyzed using linear mixed models, with statistical inference based on permutation tests applied to model residuals. The permutations tests are complete case analysis.

## Model 1
Only adjusted for subject-level covariates
```{r}

# 1                   Queensland University of Technology          0
```

# F-test
Adjusted for subject-level covariates and site-level covariates included in the randomization scheme (measured at the time of randomization).

## Complete case analysis

```{r}
# linear mixed model
fit_adj <- lmer(eortc_6norm ~ arm_c + age_baseline + ecog3 + race_gp + educ_gp + crpc_per + 
              site_country + site_timetodx + site_crpc +
              (1 | sitenew), data = analysis_data2, REML = TRUE)
# singular warning: random-effect variance for sitenew is estimated ≈ 0 in many imputations.

# main table with term p-values
main_tab <- fit_adj %>% 
  tbl_regression(label = list(arm_c = "Arm", 
                              ecog3 = "ECOG", 
                              site_country = "Country", 
                              site_timetodx = "Time from diagnosis to enrollment (site average)", 
                              site_crpc = "Percent CRPC (site average)")) %>% 
  bold_labels() 

# table of only global p-values
global_p_tab <- fit_adj %>% 
  tbl_regression(label = list(arm_c = "Arm", 
                              ecog3 = "ECOG", 
                              site_country = "Country", 
                              site_timetodx = "Time from diagnosis to enrollment (site average)", 
                              site_crpc = "Percent CRPC (site average)")) %>% 
  add_global_p() %>% 
  bold_labels() %>% # show_header_names()
  modify_column_hide(estimate) %>% 
  modify_column_hide(conf.low)

# merge tables
cc_tab <- tbl_merge(list(main_tab, global_p_tab)) %>% 
  modify_spanning_header(everything() ~ NA_character_) %>% 
  modify_header(p.value_1 ~ "**P-value**",
                p.value_2 ~ "**Global p-value**")



# hide wrong p-value for each variable
cc_tab |>
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        # Remove term p-values for variables that use global tests
        p.value_1 = if_else(
          variable %in% c("ecog2", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "site_country"),
          NA,
          p.value_1
        ),
        # Remove global p-values for variables that use term-level tests
        p.value_2 = if_else(
          variable %in% c("arm_c", "crpc_per", "site_timetodx", "site_crpc"),
          NA,
          p.value_2
        )
      )
  ) %>% 
  modify_footnote(
    p.value_2 ~
      "Global p-values obtained from ANOVA"
  )
```

Estimated marginal means, back-transformed to the original EORTC scale.
```{r}
# estimated marginal means by arm
emm_arm <- emmeans(fit_adj, ~ arm_c)

# convert to data frame and back-transform
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_arm) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_orig = inv_logit_fun(emmean),
    lower_orig = inv_logit_fun(lower.CL),
    upper_orig = inv_logit_fun(upper.CL)
  ) %>%
  select(
    arm_c,
    mean_orig,
    lower_orig,
    upper_orig
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_orig = round(mean_orig, 1),
    lower_orig = round(lower_orig, 1),
    upper_orig = round(upper_orig, 1)
  )

# create table
gt(emm_df) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Adjusted Mean Composite Scores by Treatment Arm",
    subtitle = "Back-transformed estimates from the logit scale"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    arm_c = "Treatment Arm",
    mean_orig = "Adjusted Mean",
    lower_orig = "Lower 95% CI",
    upper_orig = "Upper 95% CI"
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "Means were estimated from the mixed model and",
      "back-transformed to the original composite score scale."
    )
  )


```

## MAR
Missing data were handled using multiple imputation with predictive mean matching (100 imputations). Linear mixed models with a random intercept for site were fitted within each imputed dataset and pooled using Rubin’s rules. The bounded outcome was analyzed on the logit scale. Global p‑values for categorical predictors were obtained using ANOVA. Adjusted marginal means were back‑transformed to the original scale for interpretability.
```{r}
# there is an association between ECOG and missingness of EORTC
chisq.test(analysis_data$ecog3, is.na(analysis_data$eortc_6norm))

analysis_data %>%
  mutate(ecog3 = ifelse(is.na(ecog2), "Unknown", ecog2),
         eortc_6miss = ifelse(is.na(eortc_6norm), 0, 1),
         eortc_6miss = factor(eortc_6miss, 
                              levels=0:1, 
                              labels=c("EORTC missing", "EORTC complete"))) %>% 
  select(ecog3, eortc_6miss) %>% 
  tbl_summary(by=eortc_6miss, percent = "row") %>% 
  add_p()

analysis_data %>% 
  select(ecog3, eortc_6) %>% 
  tbl_summary(by=ecog3,
              label = list(ecog3="ECOG"))


```

```{r, results="hide", eval=FALSE}
# impute on transformed scale

# narrow down dataset to only needed variables
to_impute_mar <- analysis_data %>% 
  select(subject, eortc_6norm, arm_c, ecog2, race_gp, educ_gp, crpc_per, site_country, site_timetodx, site_crpc, sitenew)

# --- Multiple imputation
imp_mar <- mice(to_impute_mar, 
            m = 100, 
            maxit = 10, 
            seed = 123, 
            method = c(subject = "", eortc_6norm="pmm", ecog2="polyreg", arm_c="", 
                       race_gp="", educ_gp="", crpc_per="", sitenew="",
                       site_country="", site_timetodx="", site_crpc=""))
# - pmm: Predictive mean matching (numeric)
# - norm: Bayesian linear regression (numeric)
# - logreg: Logistic regression (factor, 2 categories)
# - polyreg: Polytomous (unordered) regression (factor, >= 2 categories)
```

```{r, results="hide"}
# impute on native scale, then transform

# narrow down dataset to only needed variables
to_impute_mar <- analysis_data %>% 
  select(subject, eortc_6, arm_c, ecog2, race_gp, educ_gp, crpc_per, site_country, site_timetodx, site_crpc, sitenew)

# keep eortc bounded
# set up mice
ini <- mice(to_impute_mar, maxit = 0)
post <- ini$post
post["eortc_6"] <- "imp[[j]][, i] <- pmin(pmax(imp[[j]][, i], 21), 100)"

# --- Multiple imputation
imp_mar <- mice(to_impute_mar, 
            m = 100, 
            maxit = 10, 
            seed = 123, 
            method = c(subject = "", eortc_6="pmm", ecog2="polyreg", arm_c="", 
                       race_gp="", educ_gp="", crpc_per="", sitenew="",
                       site_country="", site_timetodx="", site_crpc=""),
            post = post)
# - pmm: Predictive mean matching (numeric)
# - norm: Bayesian linear regression (numeric)
# - logreg: Logistic regression (factor, 2 categories)
# - polyreg: Polytomous (unordered) regression (factor, >= 2 categories)

# add transformed EORTC to data
imp_mar2 <- complete(imp_mar, action = "long", include = TRUE)
imp_mar2$eortc_6norm <- logit_fun(imp_mar2$eortc_6)
imp_mar2 <- as.mids(imp_mar2)

```


Model coefficients and confidence intervals were pooled across imputations using Rubin’s rules. Global p‑values for categorical variables with >2 levels were obtained using ANOVA, which combines information across imputations while accounting for correlations among category levels. These approaches address different but complementary inferential questions and are both valid under multiple imputation.
```{r}
# apply function to imputed data
fit_list_mar <- with(imp_mar2, 
                 lme4::lmer(eortc_6norm ~ arm_c + ecog2 + race_gp + educ_gp + 
                              crpc_per + site_country + site_timetodx + 
                              site_crpc + (1|sitenew), REML = FALSE))

# categorical variables (all)
cat_vars <- c("arm_c", "ecog2", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "crpc_per", "site_country", "site_crpc")

# function to extract global p-value for one variable at a time
# note: this computes anova statistic in each imputed dataset and pools these statistics using a multivariate MI combination rule to produce a single p-value (MI extension of Rubin's framework for joint hypotheses)
get_global_anova <- function(mids_obj, outcome, var) {
  formula_str <- paste(outcome, "~", var)
  miceadds::mi.anova(
    mids_obj,
    formula = formula_str,
    type = 2
  ) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("variable") %>%
    filter(variable != "Residual") %>%
    mutate(
      variable = str_trim(variable),
      row_type = "label",
      p.value = anova.table.Pr..F.
    ) %>%
    select(variable, row_type, p.value)
}

# compute each p-value
global_pvals <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    cat_vars,
    function(v) get_global_anova(
      mids_obj = imp_mar2,
      outcome  = "eortc_6norm",
      var      = v
    )
  )
)

# output table
mar_tab <- imp_mar2 %>% 
  with(lme4::lmer(eortc_6norm ~ arm_c + ecog2 + race_gp + educ_gp + crpc_per + site_country + site_timetodx + 
                              site_crpc + (1|sitenew),
                  REML = FALSE)) %>% 
  tbl_regression(label = list(
    arm_c     = "Treatment Arm",
    ecog2     = "ECOG Performance Status",
    race_gp   = "Race",
    educ_gp   = "Education Level",
    crpc_per  = "Disease State",
    site_timetodx = "Time from Diagnosis to Enrollment (Site-Level)",
    site_crpc = "CRPC (Site-Level)",
    site_country = "Country")) %>%
  # add global p-value
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x %>%
      rename(original.p = p.value) %>%
      mutate(original.p = scales::pvalue(original.p)) %>% 
      left_join(
        global_pvals,
        by = c("variable", "row_type"))) %>% 
  modify_header(original.p ~ "**P-value**",
                p.value ~ "**Global p-value**") %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_footnote(
    all_stat_cols() ~
      "Estimates pooled across multiple imputations using Rubin’s rules."
  ) %>%
  modify_footnote(
    p.value ~
      "Global p-values obtained from Type II pooled ANOVA (miceadds::mi.anova)."
  ) 

# hide wrong p-value for each variable
mar_tab |>
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        # Remove term p-values for variables that use global tests
        original.p = if_else(
          variable %in% c("ecog2", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "site_country"),
          NA,
          original.p
        ),
        # Remove global p-values for variables that use term-level tests
        p.value = if_else(
          variable %in% c("arm_c", "crpc_per", "site_timetodx", "site_crpc"),
          NA,
          p.value
        )
      )
  )

      "Inference was conducted on the transformed scale."
```

## MNAR
Participants who were deceased prior to the 6-month EORTC were assigned an EORTC score of 0.

Imputation for missing EORTC scores was done according to the methods from Carerras ACTION study method:
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12874-020-01180-y  <br>

A shift of 5–10 points was considered a small clinically important difference in EORTC, while shifts of 10–20 points were considered moderate. Accordingly, imputed EORTC scores were shifted by 0 points for ECOG 0, by approximately 5–8 points for ECOG 1, and by approximately 10–15 points for ECOG 2–4, reflecting increasing assumed deterioration in unobserved quality-of-life outcomes with worsening performance status. Using the observed mean EORTC score among ECOG 0 participants (83.7 points), this resulted in logit‑scale shifts of approximately −0.45 for ECO 1 and −0.70 for ECOG 2–4.

### Deterministic 
A controlled imputation approach was used in which imputed outcomes were shifted by pre‑specified ECOG‑dependent deltas. The shift was applied deterministically to all imputed values, representing the expected difference under an MNAR assumption.
```{r, results="hide", eval=FALSE, eval=FALSE}

# impute on transformed scale

# The paper is implementing a pattern‑mixture / reference‑based multiple imputation approach, where:
# * You impute missing outcomes under MAR
# * Then apply a clinically motivated shift (δ‑adjustment) based on a QoL variable (ECOG)
# * The shift reflects poorer outcomes for worse ECOG categories
# This is sometimes called controlled imputation.

# Conceptual Mapping to mice
# In mice, this is implemented by:
# 1) Imputing the outcome under MAR (standard regression imputation)
# 2) Post‑processing the imputed values using:
#   * ECOG score
#   * A prespecified shift (δ) per ECOG level

# create subset of needed variables
to_impute_mnar <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(eortc_6norm = ifelse(dead6==1 & is.na(eortc_6norm), logit_fun(0), eortc_6norm)) %>% 
  select(subject, eortc_6norm, arm_c, ecog3, race_gp, educ_gp, crpc_per, sitenew, site_country, site_timetodx, site_crpc)

# ECOG transformation bounded 0 to 100
######################################################################
# define ecog-based shifts - shift imputed outcome down as ecog worsens
# convert ECOG 0 mean EORTC (83.7) to a probability (0.837); logit(p)= 1.63
# calculate deteriorations on the original scale: 83.7, 76.7, 71.7, 73.7
# calculate resulting probability: 0.837, 0.767, 0.717, 0.737
# convert each probability to logit: 1.63, 1.19, 0.93, 1.03
# compute logit-scale deltas (logit_pshifted - logit_p0)
# delta_ecog <- c(
#   `0` = 0,   # 0: reference
#   `1` = -0.44, # -7: small change
#   `2-4` = -0.70, # -12: small/medium change
#   `Unknown` = -0.60 # -10
#   )

# ECOG transformation bounded 21 to 100
######################################################################
# define ecog-based shifts - shift imputed outcome down as ecog worsens
# convert ECOG 0 mean EORTC (83.7) to a probability see below (0.79); logit(p)= 1.32
# p = (83 - 21 + 0.5)/(100 - 21 + 1) = 0.79
# calculate deteriorations on the original scale: 83.7, 76.7, 71.7, 73.7
# calculate resulting probability using formula above: 0.79, 0.703, 0.641, 0.666
# convert each probability to logit: 1.32, 0.86, 0.58, 0.69
# compute logit-scale deltas (logit_pshifted - logit_p0)

delta_ecog <- c(
  `0` = 0,   # 0: reference
  `1` = -0.46, # -7: small change
  `2-4` = -0.74, # -12: small/medium change
  `Unknown` = -0.63 # -10
  )

# mild option: 0, -5, -10 
# upper option: 0, -10, -20
assign("delta_ecog", delta_ecog, envir = .GlobalEnv)

# set up mice
ini <- mice(to_impute_mnar, maxit = 0)
pred <- ini$predictorMatrix

# define a post adjustment function
# deterministic delta‑adjustment- fixed shift for each ECOG level
post <- ini$post
post["eortc_6norm"] <- "imp[[j]][, i] <- imp[[j]][, i] + delta_ecog[as.character(data$ecog3[i])]"


# run mice
imp_mnar1 <- mice(
  to_impute_mnar,
  m = 100, 
  maxit = 10, 
  seed = 123, 
  method = c(subject = "", eortc_6norm="pmm", ecog3="", arm_c="", 
             race_gp="", educ_gp="", crpc_per="", sitenew="",
             site_country="", site_timetodx="", site_crpc=""),
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  post = post
)
```

```{r}
# pooled marginal means 
# Extract fitted models
fits <- fit_list_mnar1$analyses

# Compute emmeans for each imputation
emm_list <- lapply(fits, emmeans, ~ arm_c)

# summarize emms within each imputation
emm_sum <- lapply(emm_list, summary)

# Pool estimates using Rubin's rules
Q <- lapply(emm_sum, function(x) x$emmean)   # estimates
U <- lapply(emm_sum, function(x) x$SE^2)     # variances
mi <- MIcombine(Q, U)

# Compute pooled SEs and 95% CIs (on logit scale)
alpha <- 0.05
z <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
pooled_est <- mi$coefficients
pooled_se  <- sqrt(diag(mi$variance))
lower_CL <- pooled_est - z * pooled_se
upper_CL <- pooled_est + z * pooled_se

# create data frame
emm_imp <- data.frame(
  arm_c    = emm_sum[[1]]$arm_c,
  emmean   = pooled_est,
  SE       = pooled_se,
  lower.CL = lower_CL,
  upper.CL = upper_CL
)

# convert to data frame and back-transform
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_imp) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    mean_orig  = inv_logit_fun(emmean),
    lower_orig = inv_logit_fun(lower.CL),
    upper_orig = inv_logit_fun(upper.CL)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    arm_c,
    mean_orig,
    lower_orig,
    upper_orig
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 1)))

# create marginal means table
gt(emm_df) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Adjusted Marginal Means by Treatment Arm",
    subtitle = "Back-transformed to the original composite score scale"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    arm_c = "Treatment Arm",
    mean_orig = "Adjusted Mean",
    lower_orig = "Lower 95% CI",
    upper_orig = "Upper 95% CI"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "Marginal means were estimated from pooled mixed models",
      "and back-transformed from the logit scale.",
      "Inference was conducted on the transformed scale."
    )
  )
```

### Probabilistic 
As a sensitivity analysis, a controlled multiple imputation approach was used in which imputed EORTC scores were adjusted to reflect departures from the missing‑at‑random assumption. Conditional on ECOG performance status, a pre‑specified downward shift was applied to imputed outcomes with a fixed probability. This probabilistic implementation allows heterogeneity in the magnitude of the MNAR departure while preserving the expected shift within each ECOG category.
Shift with probability p: only shift 50% of the time, conditional on ECOG
```{r, results="hide", eval = FALSE}
# impute on transformed scale

# The paper is implementing a pattern‑mixture / reference‑based multiple imputation approach, where:
# * You impute missing outcomes under MAR
# * Then apply a clinically motivated shift (δ‑adjustment) based on a QoL variable (ECOG)
# * The shift reflects poorer outcomes for worse ECOG categories
# This is sometimes called controlled imputation.

# Conceptual Mapping to mice
# In mice, this is implemented by:
# 1) Imputing the outcome under MAR (standard regression imputation)
# 2) Post‑processing the imputed values using:
#   * ECOG score
#   * A prespecified shift (δ) per ECOG level

# set up mice
ini <- mice(to_impute_mnar, maxit = 0)
pred <- ini$predictorMatrix

# define a post adjustment function
# probabilistic shifting
post <- ini$post
post["eortc_6norm"] <- "
delta_ecog <- c(
  `0` = 0,   # 0: reference
  `1` = -0.46, # -7: small change
  `2-4` = -0.74, # -12: small/medium change
  `Unknown` = -0.63 # -10
)
  p_shift <- 0.5

  shift_indicator <- rbinom(length(i), size = 1, prob = p_shift)
  imp[[j]][, i] <- imp[[j]][, i] +
    shift_indicator * delta_ecog[as.character(data$ecog3[i])]"

# another option: add random noise around the delta
# aligns with distributional interpretation in the paper

# 
#   imp[[j]][, i] <- imp[[j]][, i] +
#     rnorm(length(i),
#           mean = delta_ecog[as.character(data$ecog3[i])],
#           sd   = sigma_delta)
# "

# run mice
imp_mnar2 <- mice(
  to_impute_mnar,
  m = 100, 
  maxit = 10, 
  seed = 123, 
  method = c(subject = "", eortc_6norm="pmm", ecog3="", arm_c="", 
             race_gp="", educ_gp="", crpc_per="", sitenew="",
             site_country="", site_timetodx="", site_crpc=""),
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  post = post
)
```

```{r}
    upper_orig = "Upper 95% CI"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "Marginal means were estimated from pooled mixed models",
      "and back-transformed from the logit scale.",
      "Inference was conducted on the transformed scale."
    )
  )


```

## Compare distributions of EORTC
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# complete cases
complete_cases <- analysis_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(eortc_6norm)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "Complete case",
                ecog3 = replace_na(ecog2, "Unknown"))

# extract MAR-imputed values - 60 missing EORTC-6 * 100 imputations
long_mar <- complete(imp_mar2, action = "long") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "MAR imputation") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    was_missing = is.na(to_impute_mar$eortc_6[match(subject, to_impute_mar$subject)])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(was_missing) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ecog3 = replace_na(ecog2, "Unknown"))

# extract MNAR-imputed values
long_mnar1 <- complete(imp_mnar1t, action = "long") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "MNAR imputation - deterministic") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    was_missing = is.na(to_impute_mnar$eortc_6[match(subject, to_impute_mnar$subject)])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(was_missing)

# extract MNAR-imputed values
long_mnar2 <- complete(imp_mnar2t, action = "long") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "MNAR imputation - probabilistic") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    was_missing = is.na(to_impute_mnar$eortc_6[match(subject, to_impute_mnar$subject)])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(was_missing)


# combine all sources
eortc_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  complete_cases %>% dplyr::select(subject, ecog3, eortc_6, source),
  long_mar      %>% dplyr::select(subject, ecog3, eortc_6, source),
  long_mnar1    %>% dplyr::select(subject, ecog3, eortc_6, source),
  long_mnar2    %>% dplyr::select(subject, ecog3, eortc_6, source)
)

# density plot
ggplot(eortc_all, aes(x = eortc_6, fill = source)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of EORTC scores",
    subtitle = "Complete cases vs MAR and ECOG-adjusted imputations",
    x = "EORTC score",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# stratify by ECOG
ggplot(eortc_all, aes(x = eortc_6, fill = source)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ ecog3) +
  labs(
    title = "EORTC distributions by ECOG score",
    subtitle = "Observed vs MAR vs MNAR imputations",
    x = "EORTC score (logit scale)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_bw()


```
